text:
Minnesota arrives with points in ten straight (8-0-2), after a 5-2 win at Toronto on Nov. 12 in which Matt Boldy scored three goals. Boston is coming off a 5-2 home loss to Montreal that ended a four-game winning streak, and it is playing without James Hagens (back), who has twelve points in 17 games. Marat Khusnutdinov has taken his spot beside Lindholm and Mittelstadt. The Bruins won the first meeting in October? No: MIN won it 4-1 in Boston.

At five on five the teams are level, each with 53% of the expected goals (a measure of chance quality). The Wild create more, at 3.67 expected goals per 60 minutes against Boston's 3.19, and our model projects 3.12 goals for MIN and 2.80 for BOS. Boston takes 4.8 penalties a game, which keeps handing out power plays, and the Wild's power play averages 0.90 expected goals a game to the Bruins' 0.57. In net, projected starters Jesper Wallstedt (+16.4 goals saved above expected, meaning goals he stopped beyond what the shots should have produced) and Jeremy Swayman (+8.4) both have strong seasons. Swayman was at +26.5 last year, Wallstedt at +5.8.

Kirill Kaprizov is our top pick, with a 46% chance to score and 78% to get a point. He has a ten-game point streak, and Heather Rule of NHL.com posted that he had three assists against Toronto. For Boston, David Pastrnak leads at 30% to score and 72% for a point, with JJ Peterka a breakout name at 25%.
